# Final experiment design — ACF-based cycle-length selection for CycleNet

## 1. Objective & rationale
Evaluate whether an **autocorrelation (ACF) analysis on the training portion** can automatically recover the "right" CycleNet cycle-length hyperparameter p per dataset, and whether the recovered p matches or beats the paper's nominal values and the no-cycle baseline in forecast quality. Rationale: p is CycleNet's most consequential hyperparameter (it controls the periodic memory: phase embedding + detrending baseline), and its natural values (daily/weekly) are directly readable from the autocorrelation structure of real benchmarks.

## 2. Mechanism recap (source: public description of arXiv 2402.10322; repo is empty, no local code)
- RCF module: Transformer encoder–decoder. For each step t, cycle index s = (t−t₀) mod p → **one-hot of length p → learnable d_model×p embedding** injected as periodic/positional info into encoder (lookback) and decoder (target) tokens.
- A per-channel learnable **cycle-trend vector c ∈ R^p** is subtracted from lookback inputs (residual = x_t − c[s]) and re-added to the decoder output — so the model needs **absolute calendar time**, and the same p drives both the detrending baseline and the phase embedding.
- p must be ≤ lookback and `≪` forecast window so every phase is observed multiple times in training; a too-large p leaves most phases unobserved.

## 3. Period-estimation protocol (per training series; ACF primary, periodogram complementary)
**Detrending — PRIMARY (committed):** fit and remove a per-channel **low-order polynomial trend (degree ≤ 2)** on the training segment only; compute the ACF on the residual series.
*One-line justification:* polynomial removal suppresses trend/drift bias in r_k without the phase distortion that first-differencing introduces (my toy ACF test: first-differencing shifted the argmax 24→25). Alternative — first-difference ACF — is run only as a sensitivity check.

**ACF estimator:** r_k = Σ_{i=k..n−1}(x_i−x̄)(x_{i−k}−x̄) / ((n−k)·σ²), computed at the candidate lags (and, for the robustness check, over the full lag range 1..720 with local-max detection).

**Periodogram (complementary):** Fourier periodogram over the same detrended segment; top-k peaks (k=3) give an independent period estimate; used to corroborate p* (a p* not supported by the periodogram is flagged).

## 4. Selection rule with thresholds
**Peak selection — PRIMARY (committed):** scan only the **candidate set C** (derived from sampling resolution), pick the candidate with the **largest mean r_p** over channels:
- hourly → C = {24 (daily), 168 (weekly)} — **yearly 8760 excluded** (see caveats)
- 15-min (ETTm) → C = {96, 672}
- 10-min (Weather/Solar) → C = {144 (daily), 1008 (weekly)}
*One-line justification:* candidate-anchored scanning returns p in the exact support CycleNet can consume, avoiding the ambiguity of mapping a continuous argmax to a candidate and sidestepping un-estimable lags. Robustness check: full-lag local-max ACF peak detection (lags 1..720) mapped to nearest candidate, plus top-k periodogram peaks.

**Threshold rule — PRIMARY (committed):** a candidate is accepted only if **both** hold on the averaged-ACF: (i) statistical gate r_p > 2/√n_eff, n_eff = n−p (lag-p pair count); (ii) heuristic floor r_p ≥ 0.2. **No-cycle fallback:** if no candidate passes, use the no-cycle baseline (RCF residuals only, no cycle trend/embedding).
*One-line justification:* the statistical gate filters noise-induced spurious lags; the 0.2 floor encodes "practically meaningful" periodic strength (my toy test showed a true cycle at r≈0.89, so 0.2 is a conservative separator).

**Tie-break (channels with both daily & weekly peaks) — PRIMARY:** prefer the candidate with the higher mean r_p; if two candidates are within 0.05, prefer the **shorter period**.
*One-line justification:* shorter p is more sample-efficient (each phase observed more often per window) and daily is a sub-harmonic of weekly (24×7=168), so the residual encoder can still absorb the weekday/weekend structure that a daily cycle trend leaves behind.

**Per-series vs dataset-level — PRIMARY (committed):** **dataset-level** — average the detrended autocorrelograms across channels, select one p* per dataset via the rule above. *Justification:* CycleNet fixes one p per dataset that must serve both detrending and embedding roles, so the estimator must emit one p; averaging across channels is robust to noisy series. **Per-series assignment** (independent p per channel) is included only as an exploratory variant, evaluated with identical metrics to quantify the cost of a shared p.

## 5. Evaluation protocol (to be executed after approval, not run)
**Baselines/controls:**
1. No-cycle baseline (encoder–decoder without cycle trend/embedding) — answers "is any cycle better than none."
2. Each individual candidate p ∈ C — full factor sweep.
3. ACF-chosen p* (dataset-level, primary rule) — the proposal under test.
4. Paper-nominal p (e.g., 24 vs 168 per dataset as listed in the paper appendix) — the status-quo reference.
5. Per-series assigned p (exploratory).

**Metrics:** MAE and MSE per horizon, averaged over channels and over the 4 horizons; additionally the relative MSE reduction vs the no-cycle baseline (so the "cycle gain" is explicit and comparable across datasets).

**Splits (fixed conventions):** ETT ≈ 12/4/4 months; ECL ≈ 15/3/6 months; Traffic ≈ 7:1:2; Weather/Solar ≈ 7:1:2 (exact fractions read from the benchmark suite's configs during implementation). **Cycle is selected on the validation split only**; test metrics are reported for the chosen p* to avoid selection leakage.

**Horizons:** {96, 192, 336, 720}; **lookback fixed at 336** (assumption — see uncertainties).

**Horizon×p interaction (committed):** p is independent of horizon in parameter count, but the cycle embedding must phase-align across the **entire forecast window (up to 720)**, i.e., t mod p must map every forecast step to a phase seen in training. All accepted candidates (24/96/144/168/672/1008) satisfy p ≤ 720 and p ≤ 336-lookback with multiple phase observations per window. Exact divisibility is *not* required (t mod p handles non-divisible windows); the binding constraint is p ≪ data span, so each phase is observed often enough to estimate c[s].

**Validation & reporting:** (a) p* chosen by the primary rule on val; (b) sensitivity pane — test MAE/MSE for every candidate p and the no-cycle baseline; (c) consistency gate — p* should match the dataset's known natural periodicity (24/168 for hourly, 96/672 for ETTm, 144/1008 for 10-min); report agreement and threshold sensitivity (r_p floor swept over {0.1, 0.2, 0.3}).

## 6. Feasibility caveats (explicit)
- **Short ETT series (~2 yr) cannot support yearly lags:** lag 8760 has ~2 usable periods and lag-p ACF with n_eff ≈ 2 is pure noise; yearly candidates are **excluded from C for every dataset** on this basis.
- **10-min Weather/Solar resampling:** daily = 144, weekly = 1008, yearly = 52,560 → yearly is both statistically and memory-infeasible (cycle-trend vector would be length 52,560 with most phases unobserved in a ~336-lookback window); excluded.
- **Large p vs 336-lookback:** p=672/1008 yields <1 observed phase per window; acceptable only because many windows/weeks exist in long training sets (ECL/Traffic), but this weakens per-phase baseline estimates and motivates the dataset-level average.
- No local CycleNet code: exact configs (nominal p, split fractions, lookback) must be re-read from the paper appendix / public configs when implementing.

## 7. Assumptions & uncertainties
**Assumptions:** public CycleNet description is accurate; polynomial-(≤2) detrending adequately removes trend bias without distorting periodicity (else the first-difference sensitivity will show it); dataset-level single p is the right operating point (CycleNet requires one p for both roles); best-val-MAE is the operational definition of "optimal cycle"; the fixed 336-lookback convention; threshold values (2/√n, 0.2) are reasonable for these dataset scales.

**Uncertainties:** exact per-dataset nominal p and split fractions (unverifiable offline); whether the paper's p choice was dataset- or per-series; whether lookback is truly fixed at 336 across datasets; whether polynomial detrending suffices for strongly drifting series (sensitivity answers this); how to handle channels with no detectable periodicity under the fallback; whether "optimal" by val metric will agree with true seasonality when they conflict.

## Deliverable scope (confirmed)
Final design = rationale + mechanism recap + period-estimation protocol (ACF + periodogram) + selection rule with thresholds + evaluation protocol (baselines, MAE/MSE, split conventions) + feasibility caveats (short-ETT yearly lags, 10-min resampling) + assumption/uncertainty list. **No code, no runs** — this is a design-only deliverable.
